nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def1}
Let $A$ be an abelian group.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We define $H_i^c(X,A(n))$ to be $H_i({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)\otimes A)$.
\item We define Frobenius homology $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ 
to be the homology of the double complex 
$$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A \xrightarrow{\varphi-1} {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A.$$
Here $\varphi$ acts covariantly in
$\bar X$ on cycles on $\bar X\times \Delta^i$; the left and right hand 
complexes sit in homological degrees $1$ and $0$, respectively.
\item The Kato homology $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ 
is defined to be the homology of the complex of coinvariants
$\big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$.
\end{enumerate}

$$ \cdots \to H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\to \cdots.$$

and $i>2n+2$, and we are left with 
\begin{multline*} 
0\to H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\\
\to H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0 .
\end{multline*}
By the Weil-conjectures and counting coranks one sees that the corank $C$
of $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and of 
$H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ agree.

implies that $C$ agrees with the dimension of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$,

$H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))/{\text{\rm tor}}$ must be a lattice of the same rank.
Moreover $H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$ surjects onto the divisible part

b) $\Rightarrow$ a) We see that $H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$
is finite, because $H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\cong H^{2n}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$
\cite{ichweilI}. For the same reason, $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$
is an extension of the finite group $H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and 
a torsion divisible group of finite corank.
\hfill $Q.E.D.$
